assessment_scope: Price-blind Pass 1; enterprise analytics software and the separately identified treasury-financing activity.
overall_assessment: Mixed and leveraged. Strategy retains an established enterprise analytics software operation (now reported as the Software segment following its Q2 2026 GAAP realignment into Software and Bitcoin segments) with growing cloud subscriptions and $576.6 million in Remaining Performance Obligations. However, FY2025 software operations were cash-negative, 9M 2026 consolidated operating cash flow of +$14.267 million depended on $79.527 million of treasury interest income ($78.714 million in the Bitcoin segment), and management reiterated as of September 30, 2026 that software cash flow is not expected to satisfy near-term financial obligations. Meanwhile, the Bitcoin segment (~99% of assets; 850,849 BTC as of November 15, 2026) carries $14.110 billion of mezzanine preferred liquidation preference (~$1.51B–$1.59B annual preferred dividends plus debt interest), $5.914 billion of convertible debt holder cash puts across September 2027–September 2028, and MSCI November 2026 index-exclusion risk, alongside a November 2026 capital-allocation pivot using Class A ATM issuance predominantly to retire 12% STRC preferred stock. [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][8][9]

software_business.reporting_boundary: Effective Q2 2026, Strategy realigned GAAP reporting into two reportable operating segments: Software and Bitcoin (recasting prior periods; Q3 2026 Form 10-Q, Note 13). Within the Software segment, four revenue streams are reported—product licenses, cloud subscription services, product support, and other services—without stream-level operating-profit allocation. [1][2]
software_business.product_and_customer_evidence: The product materials describe a governed semantic layer, self-service analytics, reporting, mobile/offline access, connectors, and AI-oriented capabilities. Strategy-published cases describe enterprise use in pharmaceutical field analytics, insurance-report rationalization, retail operations, and governed AI-agent workflows. Outcome figures in the cases are company-reported and are not independent verification or a representative customer sample. [5][6][7][8][9][10]
software_business.revenue_quality: Cloud subscription revenue increased from $106.776 million in FY2024 to $175.657 million in FY2025 and was higher year over year in Q3 2026. Product support and license revenue were lower in the Q3 comparison, while the company is ending support for on-premises licenses on a published timetable. Renewal, net-retention, migration-cohort, and contract-level margin data are unavailable in the permitted evidence. [1][2]
software_business.profit_and_cash: FY2025 software revenue was $477.233 million and gross profit was $327.816 million against $368.725 million across S&M, R&D, and G&A (a derived $40.909 million pre-mark shortfall) and negative $67.241 million consolidated CFO. In 9M 2026, Software segment revenue was $372.095 million (Q3: $125.427M vs $128.691M YoY) and segment net income was $33.591 million (down from $82.740M in 9M 2025; Q3 boosted by a $503.535M income tax benefit). Consolidated 9M 2026 CFO turned positive to $14.267 million only because of $79.527 million of interest income ($78.714 million earned in the Bitcoin segment on USD Assets), and management reiterated as of September 30, 2026 that software cash flow will not satisfy near-term obligations. [1][2]
software_business.competitive_position_and_switching: The product’s potential differentiation rests on governed definitions and analytics embedded into enterprise workflows. Such integration can create migration work, but no permitted source establishes customer retention, renewal rates, displacement rates, or measured switching costs. Competitive alternatives and relative market positions are not quantified in this evidence set. [1][5][6][7][8][9]
software_business.customer_concentration: Partially disclosed in Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 13: 9M 2026 revenue was 56.2% U.S. ($208.979M), 34.8% EMEA ($129.647M), and 9.0% Other Regions ($33.469M); Germany accounted for >=10% of consolidated revenues in 3M and 9M 2026 and 2025, while no single customer accounted for >=10% of consolidated revenues. Customer count, top-10 share below 10%, and cohort retention remain undisclosed. [2][6][7][8][9]

treasury_activity.classification: Effective Q2 2026, Bitcoin accumulation, digital-credit preferred/debt financing, and USD Assets are reported as a dedicated GAAP Bitcoin operating segment (~99% of total assets; zero customer revenue; 850,849 BTC held as of November 15, 2026). [2][3]
treasury_activity.risk_evidence: Q3 2026 Form 10-Q and November 2026 Form 8-Ks expose ~$1.51B–$1.59B in annualized preferred dividends and convertible interest ($14.110B preferred liquidation preference; 12% daily-pay STRC rate), $1.046B current debt driven by $1.010B of September 2027 convertible puts (followed by $4.904B of 2028 puts), 6,947 BTC sold ($431.763M) in 9M 2026, S&P 'B-' rating, competition from spot Bitcoin ETPs and corporate treasury copycats, and expected November 2026 MSCI index exclusion. [2][3]
treasury_activity.per_share_evidence_gap: Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 11/12 quantifies 37.6% nine-month Class A share dilution (292.422M to 402.338M shares; 428.049M Q3 diluted weighted average), and November 2–15, 2026 Form 8-Ks show 74.7% ($394.6M) of $528.5M common ATM proceeds used to retire STRC preferred stock rather than buy Bitcoin (only $115.3M / 1,521 BTC), testing the seven-year BTC-per-share objective. [2][3][4]

key_strengths: A continuing enterprise analytics software revenue base with cloud subscriptions growing in the FY2024–FY2025 and Q3 year-over-year comparisons. [1][2]
Gross profit on reported software revenue and named customer use cases involving governed analytics and operational workflows. [1][5][6][7][8][9]
Direct sales, Customer Success, and a broad, generally non-exclusive partner ecosystem are described in the FY2025 filing. [1]
key_risks: Software operating cash flow remains insufficient for near-term obligations (reaffirmed as of Sept 30, 2026); 9M 2026 consolidated CFO of +$14.267M depended on $79.527M of treasury interest income, while Q3 software revenue and 9M segment net income fell YoY and on-premises support ends Dec 31, 2026. [1][2]

Heavy fixed-charge overhang from $14.110B mezzanine preferred stock (~$1.51B–$1.59B expected annual dividends plus debt interest; 12% daily-pay STRC) and $5.914B of convertible note holder cash puts in Sept 2027–Sept 2028 ($1.046B current debt), backed by an unpledged $4.75B USD Reserve (Nov 15) and S&P 'B-' rating. [2]

Capital-market competition from low-fee spot Bitcoin ETPs and corporate digital-asset treasury copycats, plus expected November 2026 exclusion from MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes (announced Oct 15, 2026), threatening passive outflows and ATM funding access. [2]

Sustained equity dilution (+37.6% Class A shares in 9M 2026; Nov 2–15 ATM proceeds used 74.7% to buy back STRC preferreds) alongside governance concentration (32.8% Class B voting power held by Executive Chairman Michael Saylor) and finance-team turnover. [2][3][4]
evidence_gaps: Software customer counts, top-10 concentration below the 10% single-customer threshold, renewal and net-retention cohorts, and on-premises-to-cloud migration counts.
Stream-level software operating costs/margins and standalone Software segment operating cash flow excluding Bitcoin-segment interest income.
Ten-year working-capital series (receivables, deferred revenue, payables) for a multi-year DSO bridge, though 9M 2026 RPO ($576.6M) and AR ($129.9M) are now captured.
Final IRS/Treasury CAMT rulemaking (September 2025 relief for unrealized BTC gains remains interim guidance) and realized MSCI November 2026 passive-rebalance impact.
Independent verification or a representative sample for customer-story outcome claims.
